Heard Mr. R.R.Soni, learned counsel appearing for the appellant as well as Mr. Sakit Ahmed,
learned Panel Lawyer for the State/respondent on the instant application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail (I.A. No. 2 of 2024).

Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the appellant is alleged to have committed repeated sexual intercourse upon the victim who was a minor girl on the date of incident, on the pretext of marriage Navin Sahu vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151662729/
1 and the victim became pregnant thrice and her pregnancy was terminated by the appellant with the help of three other co-accused persons.

sentences.text: Later, the appellant refused to marry the victim.

Learned counsel for the convict/appellant has argued that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the present case and there is no evidence on record to connect the appellant with commission of the ofence.
The age of the victim has not been properly proved that she was a minor on the date of incident.
It is a case of elopement and not forceful sexual intercourse.
The victim herself was a consenting party as is evident from her statement made before the Court.
There are no ingredients of ofence under Section 376(2)(n) of the IPC or Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
No injury has been found on the body of the victim and merely on the basis of statement of the victim, the appellant has been convicted.
The appellant is in jail since 26.02.2021 and further, the appeal is likely to take a couple of years or even more in its inal disposal, hence he prays that the appellant be enlarged on bail.

On the other hand, Mr. Sakib Ahmed, learned Panel Lawyer appearing for the State/respondent opposes the aforesaid bail application and submits that the indings arrived at by the learned trial Court is just and proper which warrants no interference as the same is based on proper appreciation of evidence.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents appended with the bail application.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case that the victim was a consenting party and she had established physical relationship with the appellant on her own will and no injury was found over the body of the victim and as per the allegation, the appellant made physical relationship with the victim from 2014 to 2021, but the FIR was lodged only on 26.02.2021 after a long delay of about 7 years for which there is no plausible explanation and further that the appellant is in jail since 26.02.2021 and further hearing of this appeal would take some time, we deem it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of the appellant.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to appellant- Navin Sahu by the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.
He shall be released on bail on his executing bail bond to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 02.08.2024.

He shall thereafter appear before the concerned trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to him by the said Court, interval being not less than 06 months, till inal disposal of this appeal.
Consequently, I.A. No. 2 of 2024 is allowed.

It is made clear that the observations made herein above are only conined for disposal of aforesaid I.A. iled in this appeal and it shall not be construed as an expression of opinion of this Court on the merits of the matter.
List this matter for inal hearing.
